title: Autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nair
ci_status: pass (one flaky test failed initially, rerun passed)
release_notes: Defaults and tooling to autotune batching/caching and quantization profiles for common workloads; adds unit-economics estimator and console recommendations; rollout behind feature flag.
description: Motivation: Per-request configuration of batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles is a large source of variance in unit cost and latency across customer workloads. Teams repeatedly re-tune these settings by hand. This PR introduces an autotune pipeline that: (1) ships reasonable defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching based on observed seq-len/throughput distributions, (2) adds curated quantization profiles and a lightweight selector that recommends profiles with predictable perf/regression characteristics, and (3) surfaces unit-economics tooling (CLI + Console) that estimates per-token cost and expected latency change for candidate configs. Summary of changes: Added runtime autotune controller that consumes sampling metrics and outputs candidate configs; added default profiles (small/medium/large workloads) for batching and caching; integrated quantization profile registry and selection heuristics; added unit-econ estimator service and console UI to show recommendations and cost delta; tests and docs. Checklist: - [x] Add autotune controller and API - [x] Add default batching/caching profiles - [x] Add quantization profiles + selector - [x] Add unit-econ estimator + Console view - [x] Add E2E and unit tests - [x] Add feature flag (opt-in) for rollout - [x] Docs and release notes Changeset highlights (high-level): - runtime/autotune/controller.go: new controller implementing sampling, scoring, and candidate generation (see commit messages for details). - pkg/serving/batching.go: new heuristics for default batch sizing based on percentile seq-length distributions (small illustrative snippet: if p90SeqLen > 1024 { defaultBatchSize = 8 } else { defaultBatchSize = 16 }). - pkg/serving/cache_profiles.go: default profiles for prefix/KV caching + TTL guidance. - pkg/serving/quant_registry.go: quant profiles registry + scoring heuristics that weigh latency, memory, and expected quality delta. - tools/unit_econ/estimator.go and cli: unit economics estimator and CLI to compute expected cost delta for a candidate config. - console/src/components/Optimize/RecommendationsPanel.tsx: UI to surface profile recommendations and estimated savings. - docs/optimize/autotune.md: new doc describing profiles, rollout strategy, and troubleshooting. - tests/autotune/*: E2E tests simulating mixed seq-length traffic and asserting cost/latency improvements. Recommend adding an 'enterprise' profile or a knob to bias toward latency over cost.","Priya Nair: Added an enterprise bias flag and unit tests that assert latency-first selection; documented in docs/optimize/autotune.md.","Ethan Brooks: Tests look good. One flake in tests/autotune/e2e_latency_test — flake appears to be timing-related. Can you make the assertion tolerant to jitter?","Priya Nair: Adjusted e2e assertions to use 95% quantile and increased retries; CI green on rerun."] CI summary: initial run: failure in tests/autotune/e2e_latency_test (timing flake), rerun succeeded. CI checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), e2e-tests (pass after rerun), lint (pass), integration (pass), perf-bench (pass, small regression flagged but within threshold). Rollout and migration notes: Feature behind feature flag autotune.v1 (opt-in by config or console). Default rollout targets: 10% of hosted API traffic in week 1, 50% in week 3, full rollout week 6 conditional on telemetry. Backout plan: set autotune.v1=false or scale controller.workers to 0; legacy behavior preserved. Migration: no DB schema changes. Config: new config.autotune.enabled, config.autotune.profiles_path, config.autotune.enterprise_bias. Monitoring: new metrics added: autotune.candidates_generated, autotune.applied_configs, autotune.rollback_count, unit_econ.estimated_savings. Security: no user data is stored; only aggregated sampling metrics used. Performance: In canary runs this saved ~18-25% per-token cost for medium-tail workloads with <5% p99 latency change. Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI. Followups: add auto rollbacks when regression > 2% in quality evals; expose per-customer opt-in via API; expand quant profiles for LLM families that use newer attention kernels.
